name: useTPU
summary: Whether on-device AI host packages are visible and what the hook actually executed.
plain: Checks which system services for on-device models are visible and reports their versions. It does not run inference or prove the TPU is active.
description: AICore hosts Gemini Nano and the TPU is reached via AICore or LiteRT. The hook reports package visibility, not model readiness or hardware usage. Unreadable package state is null. Without a benchmark there is no active delegate, so activeDelegate is null rather than claiming NPU use. AICore and Private Compute Services versions come from PackageManager, which needs a <queries> entry. Inference timings stay null here; measured model latency lives in useGeminiNano. benchmarkTPU is a JavaScript matrix multiply explicitly labelled CPU fallback.

returns.name: aicoreInstalled
returns.desc: Whether AICore is visible through PackageManager, or null before detection or when it fails; not proof of model availability.

returns.name: aicoreVersion
returns.desc: Installed AICore build. Useful when a model feature depends on a minimum version.

returns.name: privateComputeServicesVersion
returns.desc: Version of the service that delivers model weights privately.

returns.name: hasNpuFeature
returns.desc: Whether the device declares a neural processing unit feature. False on this Pixel, which does not declare it.

returns.name: activeDelegate
returns.desc: Null until the CPU-only benchmark runs, then CPU Fallback. Never a claim of current TPU activity.

returns.name: isHardwareAccelerated
returns.desc: Always false here. This hook runs nothing on the TPU.

returns.name: lastInferenceLatencyMs
returns.desc: Always null by design. Use useGeminiNano for real on-device latency.

returns.name: cpuFallbackLatencyMs
returns.desc: Duration of the last JS matrix multiplication, in milliseconds.

returns.name: isBenchmarking
returns.desc: True while the fallback benchmark runs.

returns.name: error
returns.desc: Latest package or feature detection failure, if any.

returns.name: source
returns.desc: 'hardware' when the AICore package is installed and visible; 'unavailable' when it is not installed, not visible to this app, or the native module is absent. There is no 'simulated' value.

returns.name: memoryFootprintMB
returns.desc: Always `null`: AICore does not report model memory to apps.

actions.name: benchmarkTPU()
actions.desc: Runs a 256x256 float matrix multiply in JavaScript and reports it explicitly as a CPU fallback. No part of it touches the TPU.
actions.output: Resolves with { activeDelegate: "CPU Fallback", isHardwareAccelerated: false, lastInferenceLatencyMs, throughputTokensPerSec: null, memoryFootprintMB: null }. Label it as a CPU number wherever you show it.

agentNote: Only offer on-device AI after readiness is verified separately; package visibility is not model readiness. Never present cpuFallbackLatencyMs as TPU performance; it is a JavaScript number.
